---
title: "Set up your workspace"
---

Complete this setup before beginning the guide. You will download the project files, open your workspace, and restore the R packages needed for all three examples.

Work through the sections in order. You only need to complete this setup once.

## Before you begin

Have R, Quarto, and an editor such as VS Code or RStudio installed on your computer.

## Get the project files

[Download the project ZIP](https://github.com/tmbuza/ai-assisted-microbiome-analysis/archive/refs/heads/main.zip)

1. Extract the downloaded ZIP.
2. Open the extracted `ai-assisted-microbiome-analysis-main` folder in VS Code or RStudio.
3. Open a terminal in that folder.

::: {.callout-note}
This is your **project folder**, also called the **repository root**. It contains `_quarto.yml`, `renv.lock`, `data/`, `scripts/`, and `templates/`. Run the guide’s terminal commands from this folder.
:::

## Restore the R environment

The project includes `renv.lock`, which records the R packages used for the supplied analyses.

::: {.callout-note}
### Where does code run?

Run terminal commands such as `R`, `Rscript`, and `quarto` in your terminal. After starting R, run R expressions at the R prompt (`>`). Opening a guide page does not run its code.
:::

In the terminal, start R:

```bash
R
```

At the R prompt (`>`), run:

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

if (!requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("renv")
}

renv::restore()
renv::status()
```

If asked to proceed, enter `Y` and wait for the `>` prompt before entering another command. Restore the supplied lockfile rather than initializing a new environment.

Check that the analysis packages load, then return to the terminal:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(vegan)

q(save = "no")
```

::: {.callout-note}
**If setup fails:** copy the error message. Ask AI to explain it using your R version, operating system, and the command you ran. Check the proposed fix before applying it. Keep the supplied lockfile intact while investigating.
:::

## Ready to begin?

Your terminal should be open in the project root, `renv::status()` should report no synchronization issues, and both packages should load successfully.
